findings.title: Negative cursor offset on prev pages is passed straight into queryset slicing
findings.body: In BasePaginator.get_result, start_offset is max(0, offset) for next cursors but is set to the raw negative offset when cursor.is_prev is true. Django querysets raise AssertionError on negative slice indices, so a prev cursor with a negative offset produces a 500 instead of a bad-request error. The comment claims the queryset 'will handle boundary conditions', which is false.

findings.title: Advanced-feature path allows negative offsets that bypass pagination bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result uses the raw negative cursor.offset as the slice start when enable_advanced_features is set. Negative slicing on a Django queryset fetches from the end of the result set (or errors), so a crafted cursor can read arbitrary rows outside the normal page window. The comment says 'permissions are checked at the queryset level', but the queryset filter only scopes to the organization and does not limit how far the offset can reach. This is an unauthenticated-looking bypass of pagination limits gated only on a user-controlled query flag and a superuser/global-access check.

findings.title: Undocumented query flag switches paginator and exposes new cursor behavior
findings.body: The endpoint now changes pagination behavior based on a 'optimized_pagination=true' query parameter that is not validated by AuditLogQueryParamSerializer, is not documented, and is not part of any API contract. Clients can send arbitrary cursors that now go through the negative-offset code path, which the regular DateTimePaginator rejects or clamps. This is an unreviewed API surface change.

findings.title: Clamping non-prev offsets to zero changes existing behavior for all paginators
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets to 0 for next cursors, but this change is applied to every BasePaginator subclass, not just the new one. Previously a negative offset with a next cursor was handled by the original code path; now the offset is silently rewritten, and the cursor returned to the client is computed from the clamped start, which can cause duplicate or skipped rows for existing consumers.

findings.title: Docstring claims features that are not implemented
findings.body: The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring advertises 'Streamlined boundary condition handling' and 'Optimized query path for large datasets', but the implementation is a copy of BasePaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch added. No performance optimization exists, so the docstring misleads maintainers about what the class does.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets enable reverse pagination, but the Cursor type change is unvalidated
findings.body: The new comment says the Cursor class allows negative offsets for reverse pagination, yet Cursor.from_string still parses any integer offset and nothing downstream validates it. Removing the non-negative contract from a shared cursor type affects every paginator that consumes Cursor, and the comment does not describe the risks.

findings.title: No tests added for the new paginator, negative offsets, or the query flag
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes shared BasePaginator slicing logic, and adds an endpoint code path behind a query flag, but includes no tests. Negative-offset and superuser-gated behavior are untested, so the crash and bypass risks above are not caught.
